summary: Paul Rouzer is a scholar in sinology and Buddhist studies. He has held academic posts at Harvard University and the University of Minnesota (attested 2007).

Paul Thieme (1905–2001) was an indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Göttingen (~1923–1928). He held posts at the universities of Breslau (~1936–1941), Halle-Wittenberg (~1941–1953), Frankfurt (~1953–1960), and Tübingen (1960–1973).

Paul Tillich (1886–1965) was a philosopher and religious studies scholar who studied at Berlin, Tübingen, Breslau, and Halle-Wittenberg. His career included posts at Berlin, Frankfurt (1929–1933), Union Theological Seminary (1933–1955), Harvard (~1955–1962), and Chicago (~1962–1965).

Paul W. Kroll (born 1948) is a sinologist and linguist who studied at the University of Michigan (~1971–1976). He held posts at the University of Colorado Boulder, including Associate Professor and department chairman (~1979–1990).

Paul Williams (born 1950) works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Sussex (~1969–1972) and Oxford (~1972–1978), later serving as department head at Bristol (attested 1998–2016) and visiting professor at Calgary.

Paula Kane Robinson Arai works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. She studied at Kalamazoo College and Harvard under Wilfred Cantwell Smith and Masatoshi Nagatomi, later holding posts at Vanderbilt (~1994–2001) and Louisiana State University (~2007–2021).

Pe Maung Tin (1888–1973) was a scholar in Buddhist studies, linguistics, and Indology. He studied at the University of Yangon (~1904–1909) and the University of Calcutta (~1909–1911), later serving as Professor of Pali at Yangon (~1912–1946).
Pedro Manuel Castro Sánchez is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned an MA at the University of Sunderland and studied under Peter Harvey.

Pei-jung Wu works in history, archaeology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. She completed a B.A. at National Taiwan University, studied under Hironobu Kohara, Shou-chien Shih, and Yu-min Lee, and earned a Ph.D. at UCLA under Donald F. McCallum.
Peipei Qiu is a scholar in Japanology and sinology who studied at Peking University, Columbia University, and under Paul Rouzer. She held a post at Vassar College (attested 2005).

Pema Bhum is a Tibetologist who served as a professor of Tibetan languages and letters at Lanzhou University and Indiana University, and as Director of the Latse Contemporary Tibetan Cultural Library (attested 2003–2009).

Pema Chödrön (born 1936) is a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Miss Porter's School and UC Berkeley Graduate School of Education, and under traditional teachers Chögyam Trungpa, Dzigar Kongtrul Rinpoche, and Sakyong Mipham.

Penghao Sun works in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He studied under doctoral supervisor Leonard van der Kuijp, as well as Mark C. Elliott, Charles Hallisey, Peter K. Bol, Jay Jasanoff, James Robson, Ryuichi Abe, Jie Li, Weirong Shen, and Qingying Chen.
Pentti Aalto (1917–1998) was an indologist, linguist, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at the University of Helsinki (~1934–1939) and later held a post there (~1949–1980).

Per Kjeld Sørensen (born 1950) is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Copenhagen (~1974–1981) under Erik Haarh. He held posts at Copenhagen (~1982–1993), Bonn (1991–1992), and Leipzig (1995).

Per Kvaerne (born 1945) works in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Oslo (~1968–1973), served as Professor there (~1975–2007), and was Secretary General of the IATS (~1989–1995).
Perry Link (born 1944) is a sinologist and linguist who studied at Harvard (~1962–1976). He held posts at Princeton University (~1989–2008) and the University of California, Riverside (~2008).

Perry Schmidt-Leukel (born 1954) is a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Munich (~1988–1998), Innsbruck (~1995–1997), Salzburg (~1998–2000), Glasgow (~2000–2009), and Münster (~2009–2020).
Peter Alan Roberts is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under doctoral supervisor Michael Aris and traditional teacher Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche.

Peter Bisschop is an indologist who earned his PhD at Groningen (-2004) under Hans T. Bakker and Harunaga Isaacson. He held posts at Wolfson College, Oxford, the University of Edinburgh (2005–2010), and Leiden University (attested 2011–2021).
